summary: High-level security posture discovery: Argent Capital is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployments. Key concerns: SOC2/ISO certifications, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, fine-grained RBAC, end-to-end encryption and KMS, audit log retention and export, data residency and retention policies. AE/SE explained tradeoffs and next steps include sharing SOC2 docs, scheduling an architecture deep dive, and pricing for Dedicated capacity.
topics: Encryption at rest and KMS options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:06] David (Argent CTO): David here, CTO. Priya is on for security, Marcus for platform. Jenna for compliance.
[00:12] Maya: Great. Samir and Olivia from our SE team are with me. We plan to focus on security posture and your requirements.
[00:22] Priya (Argent Sec): Thanks. To kick off, we are evaluating Redwood for inferencing across some regulated funds. Main items: SOC2, ISO, SSO (Okta), RBAC, audit logs into Splunk, KMS integration, and retention/deletion.
[00:38] Samir (SE): Understood. Quick question — are you leaning Hosted first or already considering Dedicated/Private?
[00:44] Marcus (Platform): We want to start with Hosted to get mileage but Dedicated or Private may be required for certain funds due to data residency and contractual clauses.
[00:53] Jenna (Compliance): We also need evidence for vendor attestation — SOC2 Type II is a baseline, ISO 27001 would be great. Availability SLAs matter too.
[01:05] Maya: Perfect. On SOC2/ISO: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO, we can share the report and the ISO scope summary. Samir, can you add details?
[01:15] Samir: Yeah, our SOC2 covers security and availability controls for the Hosted and Dedicated control plane. For Private on-prem, the customer controls the environment but we provide a controls mapping. Reports are redacted; we do an NDA if you want full documents.
[01:29] Priya: NDA is expected. We need to validate encryption keys — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[01:37] Olivia: Yes — for Dedicated and Private we support CMK via major cloud KMS providers and HSM integrations. Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, but you can request CMK for enterprise tiers.
[01:51] David: Clarify envelope vs CMK — we prefer CMK for production.
[01:55] Samir: CMK means you own the key lifecycle in your KMS and we reference it for at-rest encryption. Envelope is where Redwood manages the key but uses your tenant isolation. For the highest assurance, Private or Dedicated with CMK is recommended.
[02:10] Priya: For SSO/SAML we use Okta with SCIM provisioning. We need automated user provisioning and audit events for login.
[02:18] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO with Okta and SCIM for user provisioning. You can push groups which map to RBAC roles.
[02:25] Marcus: How granular is RBAC? Can we create per-team roles and limit model access?
[02:30] Samir: RBAC is role-based with resource scoping: org, project, model, route. You can create custom roles and map Okta groups. We also support token-scoped keys for programmatic access with adjustable scopes.
[02:44] Priya: Audit logs — we need logs forwarded to Splunk with retention of 7 years for certain events. Is streaming supported?
[02:52] Olivia: Yes, audit logs are exportable via syslog or cloud log sink to Splunk/Datadog. We include authentication attempts, API requests, model version used, and admin actions. Retention on Redwood side is configurable for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has default retention windows but you can export and store in your archive for long-term retention.
[03:11] Jenna: Are logs tamper-evident and do you provide integrity checks?
[03:15] Samir: We support immutable log storage for Dedicated/Private and provide HMAC-based signatures for exported log batches. For SOC2 we maintain controls around log integrity; we'll point to the specific control mapping in the docs.
[03:28] David: Data residency — some of our funds operate in EU only, and data cannot leave region. Does Redwood have region isolation?
[03:36] Maya: We have region-aware routing and private deployments that can be deployed in customer VPCs in specific cloud regions. For Hosted, we can provision in EU regions and enforce routing, but Dedicated/Private gives stronger guarantees.
[03:48] Marcus: If we do Dedicated in our AWS account, can we manage networking and subnets?
[03:53] Samir: Dedicated offers customer VPC peering or dedicated VPCs per tenant depending on the plan. Private gives you full control — deployed into your VPC or on-prem. We'll share our network architecture doc.
[04:04] Priya: Regarding data deletion, we need guaranteed deletion within X days for a tenant, including cache and backups.
[04:12] Olivia: We have documented retention and deletion processes. For Hosted, deletion requests trigger cascading delete jobs — control plane marks data for deletion and K-V caches are zeroed; however, backups may have longer retention windows. Dedicated/Private gives you stronger SLAs and options for immediate destruction if required.
[04:29] Priya: Can you support contractual language on data deletion and breach notification timelines?
[04:34] Maya: Yes, we can discuss contractual SLAs in the enterprise contract. Our standard is 72-hour breach notification, but enterprise contracts can tighten that.
[04:44] Marcus: Performance/security tradeoff — we need low-latency inference for trading signals. How does encryption/KMS affect latency?
[04:52] Samir: KMS lookups happen during key wrap/unwrap at session creation; we cache decrypted data keys in memory. Runtime path per-token is unaffected. If you require HSM in the loop per request, that would add latency; we recommend CMK with envelope encryption for minimal impact.
[05:08] David: What about model artifacts — where are they stored and who can access them?
[05:13] Samir: Model artifacts are stored in encrypted object storage with access controls. For Hosted, Redwood manages model storage; Dedicated/Private can use your storage. Access to model artifacts is restricted to runtime and authorized ops roles; we can provide an access log.
[05:29] Jenna: Can we run red-team or pen tests against the deployment?
[05:34] Maya: For Dedicated and Private yes with coordination and an approved scope. For Hosted, we have a vendor-managed testing program; we can facilitate an assessment under our testing guidelines.
[05:45] Priya: Any third-party audits or pen-test attestation?
[05:48] Samir: Our SOC2 report includes pen-test summary and remediation items. For Dedicated we can include network configuration guidance for your pen-tests.
[05:58] David: Ok — pricing question: is Dedicated billed monthly reserved and can we trial?
[06:03] Maya: Dedicated is reserved commit-based; we offer trials and pilot capacity for evaluation. We'll send pricing and trial options.
[06:11] Marcus: For Private on-prem, what's required from our infra team?
[06:15] Olivia: You'll need to provide VMs/GPUs meeting our spec, network access for control plane, and KMS/HSM endpoints if using CMK. We'll provide an install runbook and automation.
[06:27] Priya: How do you handle multi-tenancy isolation?
[06:31] Samir: We use tenant isolation at the compute and control plane levels. Dedicated gives single-tenant compute pools; Private is fully isolated by your infra. Hosted uses strong logical separation and auditing.
[06:44] David: Any notable security limitations or known tradeoffs?
[06:48] Samir: The main tradeoff is control vs time-to-value: Hosted is fastest but gives Redwood more control over ops; Dedicated and Private give you more isolation and control but require setup. Also some enterprise features like CMK and custom auditing are gated to enterprise tiers.
[07:05] Jenna: Regarding contractual indemnities and breach liability, can legal handle specifics?
[07:10] Maya: Yes, we'll route legal questions to our contracts team; I'll include a legal contact in the follow-up.
[07:17] Priya: Can you send a control mapping matrix to map Redwood controls to our SOC/ISO requirements?
[07:22] Samir: Absolutely — we'll include a control mapping and the SOC2 report excerpt under NDA.
[07:28] David: Great. What's the next step schedule-wise?
[07:31] Maya: I'll share the SOC2 and security whitepaper today. Samir will schedule a deep technical session (Marcus + SE) next week to walk private/Dedicated architecture. We'll also provide Dedicated pricing and trial docs.
[07:43] Marcus: Sounds good. One more — do you support network-level allowlists and private endpoints?
[07:48] Olivia: Yes — private endpoints, allowlists, private peering are supported for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports allowlists per API key.
[07:57] Priya: For compliance we need data processing addendum and subprocessor list.
[08:01] Maya: We'll attach the DPA and current subprocessor list.
[08:05] Jenna: Thank you, that's helpful.
[08:08] Maya: Anything else?
[08:10] David: No, that's it for now.
[08:12] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.
[08:16] -- End of recording.
